clue.text: Cape with a hat is warm…

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cape on maps
a lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Someone in a cape and a hat must be feeling hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Calid is a rare literary adjective meaning hot or heated.

clue.text: Number announced is Elgar's piece

indicators.note: announced says the drug word is said out loud, giving a similar-sounding title

parts.note: read as numb-er, something that numbs: the anaesthetic drug cocaine

explanation.surface: A numbered item on a concert programme is an Elgar work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' must be read as numb-er, a thing that numbs. Elgar's concert overture is titled after the mythical land of plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar wrote a concert overture of this name, subtitled In London Town.

clue.text: Leg ring in prison

parts.note: a leg is a limb
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A convict with a ring on his leg in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is old slang for a jail, a place of confinement.

clue.text: Corncrake, in fact, has left a track

indicators.note: in places the bird inside the word for fact, as in the phrase in deed

parts.note: a deed is a fact, as in 'in deed' versus word
the corncrake is a bird of the rail family

explanation.surface: A corncrake has really left tracks on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fact' reads as a filler phrase, but it is the container instruction: the bird goes inside a word for fact, echoing 'indeed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A train that comes off its rails has run off the line.

clue.text: -.and prevents cold starts outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for starts goes round the letter for cold

parts.note: preludes are opening pieces, starts to something
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Continuing a previous clue: something that stops cold weather setting in.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots link this clue to the one before it; 'starts' is a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to rule it out in advance, to stop it happening.

clue.text: Stuffs cushions

definitions.meaning: fills out with padding, as a verb
soft pieces of padding, as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means fills out with wadding; as a noun it means soft protective pieces.

clue.text: Uniform passed? Just!

parts.note: even means uniform, level
handed means passed over

explanation.surface: A uniform was handed over, but only just.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fair and impartial means treating all sides justly.

clue.text: Gift of frilly clothing for example

indicators.note: clothing says the frilly word dresses the abbreviation for example, wrapping round it

parts.note: lacy means trimmed with lace, frilly
eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A present of lacy underwear, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest left in a will is a gift to the heir.

clue.text: Gown with fur for evening wear

parts.note: a gown is a dress
a fur coat, the animal's coat

explanation.surface: A gown and a fur for a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailcoat worn with formal outfits at night is a garment for evening functions.

clue.text: Exhausted writer in street

indicators.note: in puts the writing tool inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A writer tired out in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up, worn out.

clue.text: People are up here for river game

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through the university town
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A town where people visit for the river and a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Students 'go up' to Cambridge University and are 'up' while in residence, so the definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: British usage says undergraduates are up at university during term, the classic case being the old university towns.

clue.text: Silly people sometimes seen going up the wall

definitions.meaning: a goose is a foolish person, so the plural means silly people

definitions.text: sometimes seen going up the wall
definitions.meaning: ornaments of birds in flight are a familiar wall decoration, flying in a line up the plaster

explanation.definitionFit: Goose is slang for a fool; and decorative flying birds climbing a wall are a known British home ornament.

clue.text: A cox in rowing is in need of oxygen

indicators.note: rowing in its sense of quarrelling signals the letters of cox in are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A coxswain out on the water gets short of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rowing' looks like the boat race but signals an anagram: COX IN becomes NOXIC, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoxic describes tissue or water lacking oxygen, a technical term for deprivation of that gas.

clue.text: Solidly-built son in tangle of shrubs

indicators.note: in places the letter for son inside the word for a tangle of shrubs

parts.note: a thicket is a dense growth of bushes
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A stocky boy caught among the bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stocky, heavily built person is described as having a sturdy, broad frame.

clue.text: Like the stars of Forest, mill about!

indicators.note: about tells us to move the letters of forest and mill round into a new order

explanation.surface: A football fan urges Forest's star players to mill about.
explanation.walkthrough: Forest is Nottingham Forest, an English football club, whose 'stars' are its players.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-based adjective means shaped like a star, star-patterned.

clue.text: The most important single monument?

parts.note: gravest means most serious, the most weighty or important
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: A question about which lone memorial matters most.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone over a burial is a memorial, a kind of monument to the dead.

clue.text: At speed, asteroid enters regions remote from Earth

indicators.note: enters says the asteroid goes into the phrase for at speed

parts.note: apace means quickly
Eros is a well-known near-Earth asteroid

explanation.surface: A fast-moving asteroid enters outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere and outer space beyond it form the realm of flight and rockets.

clue.text: Metal twisted into a locket or clasp

indicators.note: into says the letters sit inside the run of words locket or clasp

explanation.surface: Jewellery-making: wire twisted into a locket or clasp.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'locket or clasp': the end of locket, all of or, and the first letter of clasp.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a Celtic neck ring made of twisted strands of gold or bronze.

clue.text: Brightest of climbers' leaders on top of the world!

indicators.note: leaders points to the opening letter of the word climbers'

parts.note: Everest is the world's highest mountain

explanation.surface: The best mountaineers lead from the summit of Everest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleverest means most intelligent, a synonym of brightest.

clue.text: Flop about, holding one penny for a sticky sweet

indicators.note: holding means the word for flop about wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: to lollop is to move in a floppy, lolling way
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A child flopping about holding a penny for candy.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled confection on a stick, which leaves fingers tacky.

clue.text: Win attention standing next to knight

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight trying to win the king's attention while standing beside him.
explanation.definitionFit: To win wages or praise is to gain it through effort, a synonym.

clue.text: Policeman answering to a buzzer

definitions.meaning: old British slang for a constable, from the blue uniform
a large blowfly that buzzes loudly

explanation.definitionFit: The word is dated slang for a police officer and also names a common buzzing blowfly.

clue.text: Saw endless suffering in plot

indicators.note: in places the shortened word for suffering inside the word for plot

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: endless drops the final letter of the word for suffering

parts.note: hell is great suffering

explanation.surface: Someone saw endless suffering in a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheld is the past tense of behold, to look upon.

clue.text: Face-saving sort of surgery?

definitions.meaning: describes something done only for appearances, superficial

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means superficial, for show, and names the kind of surgery done to improve appearance.

clue.text: One in soft leather is an eastern ruler

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the leather word

parts.note: calf is soft leather from young cattle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man in soft leather boots rules in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph was the civil and religious head of a Muslim state.

clue.text: Bishop loose-jointed and jaunty

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
lithe means supple and flexible

explanation.surface: A supple, cheerful churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means cheerful and carefree, a synonym for jaunty.

clue.text: Rand found in money-box can be used as a bar ornament

indicators.note: found in says the currency letter sits inside the word for money-box

parts.note: a till is a cash drawer
R is the abbreviation for the South African rand

explanation.surface: Foreign coins found in a pub till might decorate the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is a musical bar, not a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a rapid alternation of two notes is a decorative flourish within a measure.

clue.text: Article advanced (of undeclared authorship)

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
on means forward, advanced

explanation.surface: An article put forward without a byline.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is short for anonymous, used of a work whose writer is unknown.

clue.text: Let learner-driver have comfort!

parts.note: L is the plate on a learner driver's car in Britain
ease is comfort or relief

explanation.surface: An instruction to allow a nervous learner to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: To let property is to rent it out under a contract.

clue.text: Circle Line hope to work for port authority, say

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: to work says the letters of line hope are set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A London Underground hope: the Circle Line working, for a harbour official.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here 'Circle' gives O and LINE HOPE rearranges to ENOPHILE. Port is the fortified wine, so a port authority is a wine expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur of wine is a lover of it, and an expert on port would be one example.

clue.text: Slips perhaps but mends life somehow

indicators.note: somehow signals the letters of mends life are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: Errors are made but life gets repaired anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: Slip is a cricket fielding position close behind the batter, so slips are examples of fielders.
explanation.definitionFit: Players in slip positions are an example of the cricket team members who stand around the ground.

clue.text: Biggles is one in story

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the word for story

parts.note: the plot is the storyline
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Biggles is a character in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: Biggles is the flying hero of W. E. Johns's British boys' adventure books.
explanation.definitionFit: Biggles is a fictional airman, an example of someone who flies aircraft.
